landmarks.name: Hanamonga na Maui
landmarks.writeup: An ancient trilithon stone structure believed to be a royal gateway built in the 13th century.

landmarks.name: Royal Palace
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the King of Tonga, located in the capital, Nukunalofa.

landmarks.name: Mapu a Vaea Blowholes
landmarks.writeup: Natural blowholes on Tongatapu island where seawater shoots through lava tubes.

cultural_events.name: Heiva Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual cultural festival featuring traditional dance, music, and sports celebrating Tongan heritage.

cultural_events.name: Tonga National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on November 4th, marking Tonga's independence from British protection in 1970.

food_writeup: Tongan cuisine centers on root crops like taro and cassava, seafood, and tropical fruits, often cooked in an underground oven called an 'umu'. Popular dishes include 'ota ika' (raw fish in coconut milk) and lu pulu (taro leaves with coconut cream and meat).
brief_history: Tonga is the only Pacific nation never fully colonized, maintaining its monarchy since the 10th century. It became a British protected state in 1900 and gained full sovereignty in 1970.

important_people.name: nAkilisi Pnhiva
important_people.description: former Prime Minister and pro-democracy advocate

current_conflicts: Tonga is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts reported as of 2024.
